rundown: Rangers beat Canadiens 3-1 at Madison Square Garden in New York, NY. Rangers led 2-1 after two periods and never looked back.
4 goals in all. Rangers's last: Scott Morrow Goal Wrist Shot, assists: Noah Laba (6), 3rd period 6:44.
Leading the way — Canadiens: Phillip Danault 1 goal, 1 pts; Lane Hutson 1 ast. Rangers: Will Cuylle 2 goals, 2 pts; J.T. Miller 1 ast.
Where Rangers won it: they outshot them 26-25.
Against the closing line (Draft Kings): Canadiens closed as 1.5-goal favorites and lost outright to Rangers; the total closed at 6.5 and they combined for 4, under by 2.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 16, 7:28 PM ET. It had Canadiens 52% and Rangers 48%, projecting Canadiens 2.9 – Rangers 2.7 (5.6 total, Canadiens by 0.1).

Final: Canadiens 1 – Rangers 3. Wrong winner: it had Canadiens at 52%, and Rangers (48%) won.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Canadiens came in with a 4% above average attack and a league-average defense (12-4-4, 3.4 scored and 3.1 allowed a game over 20 games), worth about 77 and 77 games of evidence. Projected to score 2.9, they scored 1 (−1.9 goals, 65% under); projected to allow 2.7, they allowed 3 (+0.3 goals, 9% over).

Rangers came in with a 2% below average attack and a 4% stingier than average defense (12-8-1, 3 scored and 2.7 allowed a game over 21 games), worth about 78 and 78 games of evidence. Projected to score 2.7, they scored 3 (+0.3 goals, 9% over); projected to allow 2.9, they allowed 1 (−1.9 goals, 65% under).

The bigger miss was Canadiens' scoring (-1.9 goals against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 4 against 5.6 projected (-1.6), about the 26th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±2.5).

Margin: Rangers by 2 against Canadiens by 0.1 projected, about the 80th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±2.5).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body:
NYR ML (+100) at +100: the algo gave it 48% vs 48% fair (+0 pts) — won (+1u); lost to the close (closing fair chance 48%). MTL ML (-120) at -120: the algo gave it 52% vs 52% fair (0 pts) — lost (-1u); lost to the close (closing fair chance 52%). NYR +1.5 (-265) at -265: the algo gave it 70% vs 70% fair (+0.4 pts) — won (+0.4u); same number as the close. MTL -1.5 (+215) at +215: the algo gave it 30% vs 30% fair (-0.4 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. OVER 6.5 (+114) at +114: the algo gave it 44% vs 45% fair (-1 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. UNDER 6.5 (-135) at -135: the algo gave it 56% vs 55% fair (+1 pts) — won (+0.7u); same number as the close.

The line barely moved between the algo's snapshot and the close.

No bet: nothing cleared the algo's bar before the game.

review.title: Where the public and the money were
review.body:
Splits (Action Network): spread: 40% of bets on Canadiens, 73% of the money — Rangers covered; total: 64% of bets on the over, 87% of the money — it went under; moneyline: 65% of bets on Canadiens, 77% of the money.

The sharp side by the algo's read was Canadiens, who lost and didn't cover.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.697 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +1.9 goals. It counts toward NHL scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 86 graded NHL games the algo now scales scoring ×0.940 and gives home teams -0.2 goals. Team corrections so far: Canadiens attack ×0.960, defense ×0.985 (6 games); Rangers attack ×1.017, defense ×0.960 (6 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
